summary: This document updates the registration guidance in Section 4.2 of RFC 5031, which allows service URNs with the sos service type only for emergency services offered widely in different countries. The update allows registrations for country-specific emergency services in certain cases.

plainLanguage.summary: This update allows an emergency service URN under the sos service type even when the service is offered in only one country. It replaces part of RFC 5031's registration guidance.

questions: what is the sos service urn

can a country-specific emergency service get an sos urn
subtitle: Allows registration of emergency-service URNs offered in a single country.

tldr.problem: RFC 5031's guidance limited sos sub-service registrations to emergency services offered widely in different countries.
tldr.mechanism: The updated expert guidance allows registration when an emergency service is offered in at least one country and meets the other criteria.
tldr.outcome: Country-specific emergency services can be registered under sos; RFC 5031 is updated.

today: RFC 7163 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5031. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7163.

sections.title: Why Registration Guidance Changed
sections.content:
RFC 5031 advised experts to approve sos sub-services only for emergency services offered widely in different countries. Some emergency services are initially offered in one country, so that guidance prevented their registration.

This RFC updates the second paragraph of Section 4.2 of RFC 5031.
sections.plainLanguage: An emergency service may begin in one country. The earlier guidance did not allow a URN for such a service.

sections.title: New Expert Approval Criteria
sections.content:
The designated expert should approve a sub-service only when it is for emergency purposes, offered in at least one country, does not match an existing sos service URN, and has a broadly defined description and URN to encourage reuse.

The RFC keeps the rule that sos is not for general government, public information, counseling, or social services.
sections.plainLanguage: A country-specific service can qualify if it is for emergencies, is not already covered, and its description is broad enough for reuse.

sections.title: Registry and Security
sections.content:
IANA updated the reference for the sos Sub-Services registry to point to this document instead of RFC 5031.

The RFC does not update RFC 5031's Security Considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry now points to the updated expert guidance. The existing security considerations remain unchanged.

references.text: Schulzrinne, H., "A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for Emergency and Other Well-Known Services", RFC 5031, January 2008.
